title: Streams Simulator Native Event v0.1
description: One observation emitted by a simulated world. This is the simulator's own format and owes nothing to any consumer. Consumers receive it through a declarative output adapter (output-adapter-v0.1), so no consumer's field names, timestamp rules, or record framing appear anywhere in the simulator's core. Deliberately minimal: anything a consumer could compute from the nameplate is not carried here.

seq.description: Monotonic emission sequence within a run, assigned before perturbation. Stable across regenerations of the same run, so it is a durable reference for evidence citations in a consumer verdict.

entity_id.description: Unified-Namespace shaped, e.g. 'site-a/pond-3'. The simulator's alphabet is deliberately wider than any particular consumer's; an adapter that targets a stricter consumer declares its own rewrite or rejects at adapter-validation time rather than at run time.

event_time.description: RFC 3339, UTC, nanosecond precision. The world-clock instant the observation describes.

observed_time.description: The channel's modelled link-delay arrival candidate, serialized into strict native emission order with a deterministic one-nanosecond tiebreak when needed. Always >= event_time except where a clock_skew or other delivery perturbation deliberately violates that, which is test material. Named for what it is rather than after any consumer's term for it.

value.description: Number, string, boolean, or absent for a valueless channel such as a heartbeat. Numbers are quantized to the channel's declared resolution before emission and before hashing.

unit.description: Present for numeric and counter channels, absent otherwise. Carried verbatim; the simulator performs no unit conversion and neither should an adapter.

birth.description: True when this event is part of a producer birth burst after an outage — every channel republished at one observed_time with event times spread across the gap. Modelled after Sparkplug B birth certificates. Declared rather than hidden because a real producer announces a birth; inferring it is not the consumer's job.

_forbidden_note.description: NOT A FIELD. Recorded here so review has a place to check: this envelope must never carry perturbation metadata, fault identity, hidden state, the true value behind a noisy observation, or scenario labels. An event that says it is a duplicate hands the consumer the answer to a question the whole instrument exists to ask. Perturbation provenance lives in the director-side delivery ledger.
